68713-a-history-of-the-administration-of.title: A History Of The Administration Of The Royal Navy And Of Mer
68713-a-history-of-the-administration-of.creator: Unknown
68713-a-history-of-the-administration-of.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The creation of the modern Royal Navy has been variously attributed to Henry VII, to Henry VIII, and to Elizabeth. Whichever sovereign may be considered entitled to the honour, the statement, as applied to either monarch, really means that modification of mediæval conditions, and adoption of improvements in construction and administration, which brought the Navy into the form familiar to us until the introduction of steam and iron. And in that sense no one sovereign can be accredited with its formation.

arxiv-1910-07449.title: Target Space Entanglement Entropy
arxiv-1910-07449.creator: Edward Mazenc & Daniel Ranard
arxiv-1910-07449.description: Abstract We define a notion of target space entanglement entropy. Rather than partitioning the base space on which the theory is defined, we consider partitions of the target space. This is the physical case of interest for first-quantized theories, such as worldsheet string theory.

arxiv-2104-06112.title: Bahadur efficiency of the maximum likelihood estimator and one-step estimator for quasi-arithmetic means of the Cauchy distribution
arxiv-2104-06112.creator: Yuichi Akaoka, Kazuki Okamura, Yoshiki Otobe
arxiv-2104-06112.description: Abstract . Some quasi-arithmetic means of random variables easily give unbiased strongly consistent closed-form estimators of the joint of the location and scale parameters of the Cauchy distribution. The one-step estimators of those quasi-arithmetic means of the Cauchy distribution are considered. We establish the Bahadur efficiency of the maximum likelihood estimator and the one-step estimators.

arxiv-2107-09846.title: Guided Generation of Cause and Effect
arxiv-2107-09846.creator: Zhongyang Li, Xiao Ding, Ting Liu, J. Edward Hu and Benjamin Van Durme
arxiv-2107-09846.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhongyang Li, Xiao Ding, Ting Liu, J. Edward Hu and Benjamin Van Durme. We present a conditional text generation framework that posits sentential expressions of possible causes and effects. This framework depends on two novel resources we develop in the course of this work: a very large-scale collection of English sentences expressing causal patterns ( CausalBank ); and a refinement over previous work on constructing large lexical causal knowledge graphs ( Cause Effect Graph ).

arxiv-2205-11954.title: Theoretical distribution of the ammonia binding energy at interstellar icy grains: a new computational framework
arxiv-2205-11954.creator: Lorenzo Tinacci, Aurèle Germain, Stefano Pantaleone, Stefano Ferrero, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Piero Ugliengo
arxiv-2205-11954.description: Abstract The binding energies (BE) of molecules on the interstellar grains are crucial in the chemical evolution of the interstellar medium (ISM). Both temperature programmed desorption (TPD) laboratory experiments and quantum chemistry computations have often provided, so far, only single values of the BE for each molecule.

arxiv-2411-19946.title: DELT: A Simple Diversity-driven EarlyLate Training for Dataset Distillation
arxiv-2411-19946.creator: Zhiqiang Shen, Ammar Sherif, Zeyuan Yin, Shitong Shao
arxiv-2411-19946.description: Abstract Recent advances in dataset distillation have led to solutions in two main directions. The conventional batch-to-batch matching mechanism is ideal for small-scale datasets and includes bi-level optimization methods on models and syntheses, such as FRePo, RCIG, and RaT-BPTT, as well as other methods like distribution matching, gradient matching, and weight trajectory matching.

arxiv-2501-04289.title: Defect Phonon Renormalization during Nonradiative Multiphonon Transitions in Semiconductors
arxiv-2501-04289.creator: Junjie Zhou, Shanshan Wang, Menglin Huang, Xin-Gao Gong, Shiyou Chen
arxiv-2501-04289.description: Abstract As a typical nonradiative multiphonon transition in semiconductors, carrier capture at defects is critical to the performance of semiconductor devices. Its transition rate is usually calculated using the equal-mode approximation, which assumes that phonon modes and frequencies remain unchanged before and after the transition.

pmc-10742026.title: Drug Responses in Plexiform Neurofibroma Type I (PNF1) Cell Lines Using High-Throughput Data and Combined Effectiveness and Potency
pmc-10742026.creator: Paul O. Zamora, Gabriel Altay, Ulisses Santamaria, Nathan Dwarshuis, Hari Donthi, Chang In Moon, Dana Bakalar, Matthew Zamora
pmc-10742026.description: Simple SummaryNeurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) is a genetic disorder that predisposes patients to developing nerve sheath tumors that are difficult to treat. There is currently just one drug approved for the treatment of NF1-related inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (for a limited patient population), highlighting the need for further drug discovery in this field.

pmc-11434085.title: On the Creation of a Material Bond between L-PBF-Manufactured AZ91 and Ti-6Al-4V Components in the Context of Medical Applications
pmc-11434085.creator: Lennart Grüger, Felix Jensch, Fabian Dittrich, Sebastian Härtel, Stanislaw Legutko, Szymon Wojciechowski
pmc-11434085.description: Within the scope of these investigations, the feasibility of a material bond between Ti-6Al-4V and the magnesium alloy AZ91 is analyzed. Ti-6Al-4V is frequently used for implants due to its biocompatibility, corrosion resistance, and specific strength. However, depending on the surface quality, the attachment behavior of the bone to the implant varies.

pmc-11658935.title: About Your Child’s Eating scale: a cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the questionnaire in the Greek language
pmc-11658935.creator: Andri Papaleontiou, Louiza Voniati, Alexandros Gryparis, Rafaella Georgiou, Vassiliki Siafaka, Dionysios Tafiadis
pmc-11658935.description: Feeding is an interactive process between parents and children and is related to children’s healthy nutrition, growth, and feelings about the child or parent. The effectiveness of the interaction between feeding and behaviour is strongly influenced by how well this reciprocal procedure is stimulated and supported.

pmc-12389890.title: Trends in DTP3 Vaccination in Asia (2012–2023)
pmc-12389890.creator: Ines Aguinaga-Ontoso, Laura Guillen-Aguinaga, Sara Guillen-Aguinaga, Rosa Alas-Brun, Miriam Guillen-Aguinaga, Enrique Aguinaga-Ontoso, Luc Onambele, Francisco Guillen-Grima
pmc-12389890.description: Background/Objectives: DTP3 (diphtheria–tetanus–pertussis vaccine, third dose) coverage is a key indicator of the strength and continuity of routine immunization programs, which demonstrably reduces the burden of infectious diseases globally. This study aims to assess trends in DTP3 vaccination coverage across Asian regions and countries from 2012 to 2023, focusing on changes associated with the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12816136.title: Rising burden of myopia among South Korean young adults based on 13-year trends, associated factors, and projections to 2050
pmc-12816136.creator: Yeonsu Lee, Jongwook Lee, Daeun An, Kyoung Yul Seo, Sangchul Yoon, Nathan Congdon
pmc-12816136.description: To investigate long-term and projected trends of myopia and high myopia among young South Korean males and to evaluate associated sociodemographic risk factors. A repeated cross-sectional analysis was conducted using medical records from 4,063,091 19-year-old conscripts between 2011 and 2023. Logistic regression identified myopia risk factors, while linear regression assessed temporal trends. Projection modeling estimated future prevalence through 2050.

pmc-13025144.title: Enhancing Chitosan Films for Egg Packaging Using Cellulose Nanocrystals and Sodium Montmorillonite Nanoparticles
pmc-13025144.creator: Dariush Khademi Shurmasti, Clara Mariana Gonçalves Lima, Charles Odilichukwu R. Okpala
pmc-13025144.description: Bio-based polymers are believed to often demonstrate insufficient barrier capacity and mechanical strength, especially in egg packaging processes. This current work attempted to improve the characteristics of chitosan (CS) films for egg packaging by incorporating cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) and sodium montmorillonite (MMT) nanoparticles.

pmc-13130321.title: Xanomeline-trospium: defining its place among the current antipsychotic landscape
pmc-13130321.creator: Sajitha Nair, Sukhi Shergill, Eromona Whiskey
pmc-13130321.description: Keywords: Schizophrenia, cobenfy, xanomeline-trospium, antipsychotic, muscarinic receptors SummationDescription1. Xanomeline/trospium offers a distinct therapeutic beyond dopamine receptor targeting in the treatment of schizophrenia.By selectively targeting M1/M4 receptors, it offers a unique mechanism that improves positive, negative and cognitive symptoms while avoiding dopamine-blockade-related side effects2.

pmc-13260930.title: Machine and deep learning-based forecast of Tehran’s accelerating nighttime surface heat island crisis
pmc-13260930.creator: Motahhareh Zargari, Sarmad Ghader, Isidro A Pérez, M Ángeles García
pmc-13260930.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The nighttime Surface Urban Heat Island (SUHI) phenomenon in the metropolis of Tehran poses severe risks to urban climate and sustainability, representing a potential crisis for the entire Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. A critical research gap persists in long-term predictive modeling for rapidly urbanizing arid regions like Tehran, particularly using advanced hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) architectures that integrate spatial and temporal learning.

pmc-13289067.title: Help-seeking and barriers to emergency care during out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in public housing areas: a qualitative study
pmc-13289067.creator: Anne Juul Grabmayr, Astrid Marie Rolin Kragh, Sofie Kjærholm, Annam Pervez Sheikh, Doris Østergaard, Christian Hassager, Fredrik Folke, Tine Tjørnhøj-Thomsen, Carolina Malta Hansen

pmc-13297172.title: Tuning the Fire: Context-Dependent Mitochondrial ROS Signaling, Mitohormesis, and Redox-Modulating Interventions
pmc-13297172.creator: Evelina Charidemou, Eleni Andreou, Christos Papaneophytou
pmc-13297172.description: Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) are central regulators of cellular function, yet their biological roles are often reduced to an oxidative-stress/antioxidant dichotomy. This review reframes mtROS through the concept of mitohormesis, in which outcomes are neither inherently harmful nor beneficial but are determined by a defined set of contextual variables.

pmc-13321765.title: Next of kin involvement in mental health care services – a systematic participatory overview of evidence syntheses
pmc-13321765.creator: Peggy Prien, Sebastian Bayer, Susanne Kappesser, Nora Dietrich, Sven Speerforck, Johanna Kummetat, Sarah Schernau, Silvia Bahl, Franziska Vosseberg, Kolja Heumann, Sebastian von Peter
pmc-13321765.description: BackgroundThe importance of the involvement of next of kin (NOK) in mental health treatment settings is widely recognized. Yet, interventions to involve NOK are not sufficiently implemented in clinical practice – a situation that the German-based collaborative-participatory research project “Involvement of Next of Kin in Psychiatric Care” (PazAng) aims to change.

pmc-13575982.title: Bergamot (Citrus bergamia) Supplementation and Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13575982.creator: Mahla Chambari, Helia Mardani, Marjan Roshandel, Hossein Rafiei, Whitney Linsenmeyer, Maryam Jafari, Vaidehi Ulaganathan, Ali Jafari
pmc-13575982.description: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality. Bergamot ( Citrus bergamia ), a flavonoid‐rich nutraceutical, has shown potential cardiometabolic benefits, yet evidence from human trials remains inconsistent. This systematic review and dose–response meta‐analysis evaluated the effects of bergamot ( Citrus bergamia ) on cardiovascular disease risk factors in adults.

pmc-13616607.title: Phylogenetic analysis and sex identification of captive African grey parrot (Psittacus erithacus) in Uganda and Japan
pmc-13616607.creator: Nami SUZUKI-HASHIDO, Sayaka TSUCHIDA, Dickson NDOBOLI, Steven KAKOOZA, Brian MUHINDO, Victor MUSIIME, Barbara ALAPO, Mina AOYAMA, Daisuke MORI, Hitoshi MURAI, David MUSINGO, Kazunari USHIDA
pmc-13616607.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The African grey parrot (Psittacus erithacus) is endangered due to habitat loss, poaching, and illegal trade. In 2022, Chubu University and the Uganda Wildlife Education Centre–Conservation Area (UWEC-CA) have initiated an ex-situ conservation project for rehabilitation and future reintroduction. Noninvasively genetic sampling was conducted using feces from four parrots at UWEC-CA and naturally shed feathers from 22 parrots at 11 Japanese zoos. Non-invasive genetic sampling enabled reliable sex identification and mitochondrial sequencing of parrots in Uganda and Japan.
